bottleneck: Sequencing every newborn could catch treatable genetic diseases before symptoms, but it also reveals adult-onset risks, carrier status, and variants of uncertain significance in children who cannot consent. Storage of lifelong genomic data creates privacy risks spanning a century, and the psychological burden on families of ambiguous findings is real and lasting. No consensus exists on what to report, who decides, or how to handle incidental findings that affect relatives.
current_state: Pilot programs sequence newborns for expanded panels in several countries, but universal newborn genome sequencing remains ethically contested and unadopted. Policy debates outpace the technology.

title: Newborn genome sequencing stalled on consent ethics
why_it_blocks: Early detection saves lives only if the program exists. Ethical deadlock over consent, privacy, and reporting keeps a proven technology out of the nursery while treatable babies go undiagnosed.
